source: opus C1 (stand-in, flash slot) + fable I-3 (stand-in, astra slot)
text: The proposed CONTROL test cannot fail. In `addlast(actions) { action(NewAction) { trigger OnAction() } }` the inner `action_declaration` has a `name` field, so the generic arm makes IT the member and shadows whatever the anchor wrapper contributed. The test passes on master today and also passes under the exact mutation it claims to guard (widening the arm/fallback to the whole *_modification family).

source: opus C2 (stand-in, flash slot) + fable I-1 (stand-in, astra slot)
text: The design delivers only the `identify` half of the issue's Capability line and leaves a doc comment that its own commit makes FALSE. `root_classification.rs:176-180` states action modifications 'could not be fixed by adding a fifth string here' BECAUSE 'the lowerer never captures it as an enclosing member at all' -- true today, false the moment the lowerer change lands. Meanwhile `is_page_action_wrapper` (:181-189) still rejects `modify_action_modification`, so the trigger gains a member for identity but still no `page-action` kind.
evidence: Read at source: the four-string match and the KNOWN GAP paragraph are exactly as quoted. Resolution (a) taken: `modify_action_modification` joins the match, a hand-stated unit test pins the classification, and the KNOWN GAP paragraph is rewritten as closed in the same commit.

text: The blast radius was scoped to L3 stable ids only. The IR field also feeds the program engine's `RoutineNodeId` (`source_routine_node_id`, enclosing_member_lc). Today two sibling action `modify()` blocks each declaring `OnAfterAction()` mint the SAME node id and one is dropped by run-collapse; after the fix they are distinct. That de-collision is the real product value and nothing in the proposed test set observes it.
evidence: `sig_fp.rs:155-166` reads `decl.enclosing_member` verbatim; `ids.rs:314-330` discriminates the stable id on the member. A new test beside `tests/cli/cli_p1_enclosing_member.rs`'s two-field case pins two distinct ids for two action modifies. No golden directory involved. FINAL PANEL: the program-engine half is no longer only transitive -- C3 pins source_routine_node_id directly (D10).

text: P3's justification (copied from the existing source comment) is factually wrong about AL: an `addfirst`/`addlast`/`add` target is the CONTAINER the new members go inside, not an anchor naming a different member, and `addfirst_views_modification`/`addlast_views_modification` have no required target at all. The scope conclusion survives, but on different grounds.
evidence: node-types.json re-read: `addfirst_views_modification fields={'body': ['views_mod_body']}` -- no target. Corrected reason, in the ledger and in the source comment: an `add*` body DECLARES its own named members, so any routine inside finds its declaring member through the ordinary name gate; the wrapper's target -- anchor or container -- is never that routine's declaring member. ROUND 2: opus re-raised the REPLACEMENT wording, and fable's N1 said the same independently -- 'an add* body declares its own named members' is falsified by v2's OWN control fixture, where a trigger sits directly in the body and no member is declared at all. Final wording, in the ledger and in lower/mod.rs: an add*/move* wrapper's target is never the declaring member of a routine in its body -- either the body declares that member itself (the ordinary name gate finds it) or the routine sits directly in the body and has no declaring member (None, pinned by the control test). modify is the only form whose target IS the member the body belongs to.

source: opus I3 + fable P4-extension (stand-ins); count corrected by the conductor
text: P4's scan covered only `tests/**/*.al`, missing inline AL inside Rust tests and saying nothing about the CDO baseline the merge gate runs. The 'no golden moves' claim needed a wider basis.
evidence: Re-scanned: every `.al` and `.rs` under the worktree (no action modification anywhere; the `modify(` hits are all `Rec.Modify()` calls) and the pinned CDO baseline, brace-matched and comment/string-stripped: 246 actions sections, 113 action-`modify` blocks, ZERO containing a trigger or procedure. fable reported 128 blocks and opus 113; the conductor's own scan says 113, so fable's number is not adopted. text: A malformed `modify() { trigger ... }` parses with a PRESENT, zero-width `target`, so the fallback mints `enclosing_member: Some(("", origin))`. `Some("")` takes the discriminated arm in `to_stable_routine_id_from_parts`, giving the routine a different, meaningless stable id than the same routine with no member. Pre-existing for `modify_modification`.
evidence: Real parse confirms `target: (identifier [10,15]-[10,15])` on `modify()`. Fixed at the shared fallback with an is-empty filter, mirroring `dataitem_table_name` (`lower/mod.rs:668-672`), which already filters for exactly this reason -- so both kinds are covered by one guard. ROUND 2: the guard is raised one rung (a .filter on the whole enclosing_member) so it also covers the Name path -- action_declaration.name is a REQUIRED field, so tree-sitter recovery inserts a present zero-width node there by the same mechanism (opus B3). Twin empty-target test for modify_modification as well (fable M3), and the empty tests assert the routine was still found (routines.len() == 1) so a future parse collapse cannot make them vacuous (opus B5).

text: Test 1 used `trigger OnAction()` on a MODIFIED action; a modify carries OnBeforeAction/OnAfterAction. The lowerer does not validate, so it would pass, but an uncompilable fixture misleads the next reader.

source: code-review agent I1, co-signed by both stand-ins

source: code-review M2, co-signed by both stand-ins
text: The control test's doc and the fallback comment both claim the control pins the FALLBACK's scope. It cannot: collect_routines never passes an add* node as member, so the fallback is unreachable for that family and widening it alone leaves the control green. What the control pins is the PAIR of sites.
evidence: Both wordings corrected; the D3 record (two scripted edits) is what shows the pair is the real unit.

text: The empty-guard comment blamed 'tree-sitter recovery' for the zero-width node. There is no recovery: both shapes parse CLEAN (no ERROR, no MISSING, has_error() false), so ParseStatus stays Clean and nothing downstream flags them. A reader taking the comment at face value could conclude the diagnostics already cover it and revert the filter as redundant.
evidence: Re-verified by the conductor: `tree-sitter parse` exits 0 with zero ERROR/MISSING nodes for both `modify()` and a nameless `action()`. Comment rewritten to say what actually happens. The grammar accepting a zero-width identifier in a required field is filed as a discovery -- we own tree-sitter-al. ROUND 2: opus RE-RAISED -- the fix was one file short. The [Unreleased] CHANGELOG bullet still said the two paths are 'both of which tree-sitter recovery can leave zero-width', the very claim C5 falsified, in exactly the shape B2 was raised for. Corrected: the grammar can leave a REQUIRED field zero-width with no ERROR, no MISSING and no ParseStatus signal, so nothing else catches it.
